correctness.rationale: Reflection counts the middle bridge between two fixed admissible boundaries. With t=2n-a-b and binomial offsets d1=(y-x)/2, d2=(y+x+2)/2, the fixed-offset Stirling expansion has correction -(2d^2+1/4)/t, so the leading difference uses d2^2-d1^2=(x+1)(y+1); dividing by the Catalan count gives the stated product with O(n^-1) error, including odd t. Under fair independent letters a linear set of disjoint interior blocks makes any fixed type fail saturation with exponentially small probability, and dividing by the polynomial Dyck probability preserves exponential decay. Hanf locality on the bounded-degree directed successor path (with the unary colour) then leaves only truncated neighbourhoods determined by finite endpoint windows. Every admissible pair has positive mass, which both terminates the finite search for saturated completions and forces exponentially small errors for limits 0/1. In even prefix length 2m≥4 the numerator weights are odd; two weights 1 and at least one of each increasing odd weight ensure the sorted subset-sum interval condition, proving surjectivity onto all dyadics. First prefix UD has limit 1/4. This proof is for fixed sentences in the given signature, not full order or matching. Independent bounded replay: python3 /workspace/branches/reproduction/dyck.py; DP matched the reflected formula at 5084 positions and verified the sorted-weight criterion through length 20; the finite checks are not the general proof.
